_comment: OpenSSF Best Practices badge (passing level) proposed answers for Scratchsmith. Read by bestpractices.dev when the project entry is edited / re-run with 'Save (and continue)'. Status values: Met | Unmet | N/A ('?' / unknown are ignored). Justifications are a starting point; the authorized maintainer reviews and confirms each before saving. Repository: https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith
description_good_justification: The README and documentation site describe up front what Scratchsmith does: a daemonless supply-chain packager that turns a prebuilt dynamic glibc Linux ELF into a minimal, non-root FROM scratch OCI image with an SBOM and ELF-hardening lint. https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith
interact_justification: Users can ask questions and interact via GitHub Issues: https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/issues
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md at the repository root explains how to contribute: https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the requirements for contributions: PR-only with conventional-commit PR titles, passing CI (cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, tests, coverage floor), resolved review threads, and a changeset fragment for user-facing changes. https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
floss_license_justification: Released under the MIT License, an OSI-approved and FSF-recognized FLOSS license.
license_location_justification: The license is in the standard LICENSE file at the repository root: https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/blob/main/LICENSE
documentation_basics_justification: The README plus a versioned documentation site cover installation, verification, configuration, and usage: https://schubydoo.github.io/scratchsmith/
documentation_interface_justification: The external interface — the CLI subcommands (pack, lint, doctor) and their flags — is documented in the README, the docs site, built-in --help, and generated shell completions. https://schubydoo.github.io/scratchsmith/
sites_https_justification: The project repository (github.com) and documentation site (schubydoo.github.io) are served exclusively over HTTPS.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests provide discussion of proposed changes and issues that is searchable, addressable by URL, and does not require client-side JavaScript. https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/issues
english_justification: All documentation and project communication are in English.
maintained_justification: The project is actively maintained; changes ship regularly through reviewed pull requests (latest release v0.2.0).
repo_public_justification: The source is in a public git repository: https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith
repo_track_justification: git records what changes were made, who made them, and when.
repo_interim_justification: Interim development versions are publicly available between releases as commits on the main branch.
repo_distributed_justification: The project uses git, a distributed version control system.
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique version identifier, set in Cargo.toml and the git tag (e.g. v0.2.0).
version_semver_justification: Releases follow Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 (pre-1.0: breaking changes bump the minor).
version_tags_justification: Every release is a git tag of the form vX.Y.Z, and release tags are protected against deletion/force-push by a repository ruleset.
release_notes_justification: Each release has human-readable notes in CHANGELOG.md and on the GitHub Releases page, generated from changeset fragments by knope. https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerabilities have been fixed to date; changesets reserve a dedicated `security` category for such fixes when they occur.
report_process_justification: The process for reporting bugs (GitHub Issues) is documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and the issue tracker: https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/issues
report_tracker_justification: Bugs are tracked in GitHub Issues.
report_responses_justification: The maintainer responds to bug reports filed as GitHub Issues.
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests filed as GitHub Issues receive responses, including a decision when a request is declined.
report_archive_justification: The bug report history is publicly archived and searchable in GitHub Issues: https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/issues
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md documents how to report vulnerabilities: https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Vulnerabilities can be reported privately via GitHub private vulnerability reporting (Security tab) and the contact in SECURITY.md: https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith/security/advisories
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging a vulnerability report within a few days (best-effort for a solo, side-project OSS tool).
build_justification: The project builds from source with `cargo build`.
build_common_tools_justification: It is built with Cargo, the standard and widely available Rust build tool.
build_floss_tools_justification: The build uses only FLOSS tools (cargo, rustc; release cross-builds use zig via cargo-zigbuild, also FLOSS).
test_justification: An automated test suite runs with `cargo test` / `cargo nextest run` (unit + integration); CI enforces a line-coverage floor (`cargo llvm-cov --fail-under-lines 90`).
test_invocation_justification: Tests are run via the standard `cargo test` (or `cargo nextest run`), documented in CONTRIBUTING.md.
test_most_justification: The test suite covers most of the code: CI enforces a >=90% line-coverage floor (`cargo llvm-cov --fail-under-lines 90`) and tracks per-PR patch coverage via Codecov.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: CI runs the full test suite on every pull request and push (GitHub Actions), including an MSRV build and a static-musl link check.
test_policy_justification: Project policy requires tests for major new functionality; this is documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and enforced by the coverage floor and patch-coverage checks.
tests_are_added_justification: New functionality is accompanied by tests; the CI coverage floor and Codecov patch-coverage check enforce this on every PR.
tests_documented_added_justification: The policy of adding tests with new functionality is documented in CONTRIBUTING.md.
warnings_justification: Compiler and linter warnings are enabled (cargo build warnings plus clippy), and rustdoc lints run with -D warnings.
warnings_fixed_justification: Warnings are treated as errors: CI runs `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, so code with warnings cannot merge.
warnings_strict_justification: The project builds with maximally strict warnings: clippy with `-D warnings` across all targets and features, plus `cargo fmt --check` and typos.
know_secure_design_justification: The design applies secure-design principles: images are non-root (UID 65532) and minimal (FROM scratch), inputs are validated (goblin ELF parsing, glibc-only enforcement, deterministic ld.so path resolution, dlopen-gap detection), and external tools (cosign, syft, ldconfig) are invoked with argv vectors — never shell strings — so untrusted values are not shell-interpolated.
know_common_errors_justification: Implemented in Rust (memory-safe by default). The known-risk areas — path handling during dependency resolution/staging and invocation of external tools — are explicitly guarded (argv Command vectors, no shell interpolation) and covered by tests.
crypto_published_justification: Cryptographic use is limited to publicly published, expert-reviewed mechanisms: Sigstore/cosign for keyless signing and SLSA provenance, SHA-256 for checksums and OCI content digests, and rustls (TLS 1.2/1.3) for registry connections. No bespoke cryptography.
crypto_call_justification: Cryptographic functionality is delegated to established FLOSS software and crates (cosign/Sigstore, the sha2 crate, rustls + aws-lc-rs); nothing is reimplemented.
crypto_floss_justification: All cryptographic dependencies (cosign/Sigstore, sha2, rustls, aws-lc-rs) are FLOSS.
crypto_keylength_justification: Scratchsmith manages no long-term cryptographic keys; image and artifact signing use cosign keyless (Sigstore short-lived certificates via OIDC).
crypto_working_justification: No broken cryptographic algorithms (e.g. MD5/SHA-1 for security, single DES, RC4, Dual_EC_DRBG) are used; digests are SHA-256.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No cryptographic hash with known collision weaknesses is used for security purposes (SHA-256 throughout).
crypto_pfs_justification: Registry connections use rustls, whose default cipher suites provide perfect forward secrecy (TLS 1.3, and ECDHE for TLS 1.2).
crypto_password_storage_justification: Scratchsmith stores no user passwords and has no user accounts; registry credentials are read from the user's existing Docker config at push time and never persisted by scratchsmith.
crypto_random_justification: Scratchsmith generates no security-sensitive random values itself; signing entropy is handled by cosign/Sigstore.
delivery_mitm_justification: Releases are distributed over HTTPS with SHA-256 checksums, cosign/Sigstore signatures, and SLSA build-provenance attestations; the GHCR image is a signed multi-arch image. Verification steps are documented. https://github.com/schubydoo/scratchsmith#verifying-releases
delivery_unsigned_justification: All documented install methods use HTTPS, and release artifacts are cryptographically signed (cosign) with a verifiable SHA-256 checksum and SLSA provenance.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no known unpatched vulnerabilities; dependencies are monitored with cargo audit, cargo deny, and Renovate (with a supply-chain release-age cooldown) and updated promptly.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No unpatched critical vulnerabilities exist; supply-chain auditing (cargo audit/deny) and code scanning (CodeQL) run in CI.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No valid credentials are committed to the repository; gitleaks scans every push and GitHub secret scanning is enabled.
static_analysis_justification: Static analysis runs in CI: clippy (`-D warnings`), CodeQL, cargo audit, cargo deny, zizmor (workflow auditing), and OpenSSF Scorecard.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL and cargo-audit look for common vulnerability classes; zizmor audits GitHub Actions workflows for common misconfigurations.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Medium-and-higher static-analysis findings are fixed before merge; clippy warnings are hard errors in CI.
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis runs on every pull request and push, plus scheduled Scorecard and CodeQL runs.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No fuzzing or sanitizer-based dynamic analysis is set up yet. The codebase is memory-safe Rust and exercised by integration tests that run the real binary (including a smoke-run and a static-musl link assertion), but continuous fuzzing (e.g. cargo-fuzz / ClusterFuzzLite) is a candidate follow-up. Dynamic analysis is a SHOULD, not a MUST, at the passing level.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: No dynamic analysis is performed yet, so there is no sanitizer configuration to report; the code is memory-safe Rust with no `unsafe` in the core paths.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No dynamic analysis is performed yet.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic-analysis defects exist because no dynamic analysis is performed yet.
